name: Backfit the per-reporter offset; subtract the habit
delivery_mode: ESCALATED -- not delivered, not committed to src/
reason: A correct implementation of this step, built against 06 section 5.2 and adr-per-reporter-offset-estimator in full, turns FIVE acceptance tests from three earlier slices red. Repairing five oracles in one step is the shape the test-integrity rule exists to catch, so the work was reverted rather than landed and the decision is handed back. The branch is green at 04-04. Nothing under src/ carries any part of this step.
what_was_built_and_reverted: The full step, RED first and then GREEN on its own tests: shrinkTowardZero in estimate.ts; withReporterOffsets (06 section 5.1's `mid - u_hat` seam) and backfitReporterOffsets in weights.ts; REPORTER_OFFSET_TAU = 4 and BACKFIT_PASSES = 3 in constants.ts; the weighing room frozen before the loop and the backfit wrapping the pooling ladder in correction-file.ts; an acceptance file and six unit laws. The whole diff is preserved beside this contract as 04-05-attempt.patch so nothing has to be rediscovered. Its own tests were passing at the unit layer; what it broke was other slices.

what_the_authorities_say: 06 section 5.2 and adr-per-reporter-offset-estimator decision 2: u_hat = (n_r / (n_r + tau_u)) * u_raw, tau_u = 4, shrunk toward ZERO. No re-centring is mentioned anywhere, and shrinking toward zero rather than toward a population mean is stated as load-bearing.

adr-per-reporter-offset-estimator, Alternatives considered, row 4: 'Hard threshold (offset ignored below n reports, raw above)' is REJECTED, because '09 section 5.4's whole point: shrinkage removes the cliff'. So the offset is estimated for EVERY reporter, not only for those with enough history to be identifiable.
adr decision 4: u_r 'is subtracted inside the residual computation only', which is 06 section 5.1's r_height = H_eff_pred - (mid - u_hat) -- upstream of every weight and every gate.
the_contradiction.what_follows_arithmetically: Because every reporter gets an offset, and because an offset shrunk toward zero (rather than re-centred) does not sum to zero over a key's samples, EVERY key's stored difference and stored standard error move the moment this step lands -- in any fixture where a reporter's own mornings do not average exactly to their key's mean. That is every fixture this feature has. It is not a bug in the implementation; it is what the estimator is.
the_five_tests_that_go_red: tests/acceptance/f-forecast-learns-from-the-beach/gate-passes-and-shrinks.test.ts (01-08): 'stored error 0.08675985665774655 must equal the fixture's own standard error 0.08954430086935639'. The fixture computes se from its own unshifted residuals; the fit now computes it from offset-corrected ones. A 3 per cent move.

tests/acceptance/f-forecast-learns-from-the-beach/shrink-corridor.test.ts (01-13): 'keeps every generated stored height difference between its raw value and zero'. THIS ONE IS A PROPERTY, NOT A PINNED NUMBER, which is why it is listed first among the reasons to stop: the corridor is measured against a raw difference the test computes from the mornings it wrote, and an offset-corrected fit can legitimately land outside it. Either the corridor's definition of 'raw' has to change, or the invariant is genuinely weakened.
tests/acceptance/f-forecast-learns-from-the-beach/three-proven-spots-become-a-family.test.ts (03-03): pooling corridor computed from unshifted residuals.

tests/acceptance/f-forecast-learns-from-the-beach/pooling-steps-aside-once-eight-spots-differ.test.ts (03-04): 'with only seven proven spots spot-0 must be pooled at the hand-set prior (0.12 from its own mornings), not at 0.1528018557511187'. Its fixture gives each device two mornings of the SAME parity, so every reporter is maximally unbalanced and the offsets are large.

tests/acceptance/f-forecast-learns-from-the-beach/chronic-disagreement-is-down-weighted-never-silenced.test.ts (04-03, authored this session): the newcomer guard, 'the same morning stored -0.066716531924113 reported by a stranger and -0.12530241391493974 reported by a familiar face'.
the_contradiction.the_newcomer_guard_is_a_different_kind_o: The roadmap records 'A newcomer's first morning enters at full voice' as green at authoring and says it must stay green (GDP-10, the Sybil argument). It is not numeric drift. But 06 section 5.2's own table says a reporter at n_r = 0-1 has their 'report enter near face value' while a reporter at n_r = 16 has their habit mostly subtracted -- so the two ARE treated differently by design, and no implementation of this step can make a stranger's morning and a familiar face's morning produce the same stored number. The reading that survives is that 'weighs' governs the WEIGHT, which 04-03's unit property already holds directly and independently of this step ('a reporter nobody has ever co-observed keeps a full voice', proven against a loudly disagreeing community). Whether that reading is accepted, and therefore whether that acceptance example's oracle may be re-expressed, is not a call this step should make on its own.

the_two_candidate_readings: (A) THE ESTIMATOR IS RIGHT AND THE FIVE ORACLES ARE STALE. Every one of them pins a number computed from residuals formed before this stage existed; their CLAIMS all survive (the gate still passes, pooling still steps aside, the corridor still binds) and only their arithmetic moved. Cost: five acceptance oracles across four slices rewritten in one step, three of them from slices verified green at 474/474, and 01-13's corridor property needs its notion of 'raw' redefined rather than recomputed. That is a large deliberate cross-slice decision, not a step's worth of repair.

(B) THE ESTIMATOR NEEDS A CONSTRAINT NOBODY HAS WRITTEN DOWN. The obvious candidate is re-centring the offsets so they sum to zero over each key's samples, which would make each key's stored DIFFERENCE exactly invariant. It would NOT keep all five green: 01-08 pins the stored standard error, which is the weighted sample deviation of the SHIFTED values and moves even when their mean is exactly preserved. Re-centring narrows the damage, it does not remove it. It was considered and rejected here on its merits, not for convenience: if the weighted mean of u over a key's samples is zero then the key's mean is EXACTLY unchanged, so the habit would never be subtracted from any stored number and criterion 2 of this very step could not hold. Re-centring and 'subtract the habit' cannot both be true. If some third constraint is intended, it is not in 06 section 5.2, not in the ADR, and not in the roadmap.
recommendation: Reading (A), taken as its own deliberate piece of work rather than folded into this step: land the estimator, then repair the five oracles one file at a time, each with its own falsifiability pass, and re-derive 01-13's corridor against the offset-corrected raw rather than the reported one. That sequencing keeps every repair individually reviewable, which is exactly what doing five at once destroys. It needs an explicit go-ahead because it rewrites acceptance surface from three earlier slices.
also_found_and_fixed_in_the_attempt: n_r must count REPORTS, not samples. 06 section 5.2's table is stated per report ('n_r (reports by one person)', 'se(u_raw) ~ 0.48/sqrt(n_r)') and tau_u is derived from per-report noise, but one report pairing against two forecast models produces two samples. Counting samples under-shrinks a reporter whenever more than one model covers their morning. The fix is in the preserved patch. It does not affect any current fixture, all of which carry a single source, and it is not the cause of any of the five failures. KNOWN DEFECT IN THE PRESERVED PATCH, recorded rather than left to be inherited: the patch identifies a report by `${day} ${device_id}` and an UNDATED sample therefore has no distinguishing part, so every undated sample from one device collapses into a single counted report. That is the opposite of the rule 04-01 established and defended -- a sample whose day cannot be read is its own session, never merged with another -- and the report key needs the same treatment before the patch is resumed from. It is what made the three-pass unit example read n_r = 1 where the fixture meant 4, since that fixture's samples carry day: null.
red_evidence: The acceptance file was written first and run against the 04-04 body. Its oracle was validated at RED by the check the reviewer asked for: with no estimator in the code the measured share of full trust came out at 0.9999999999999997, within a billionth of 1.0, which proves the hand-computed counterfactual, the two-coast basin partition and the shrink-is-the-identity assumption together. The six unit laws were RED against the absent functions and GREEN against the implementation, including one example pinning three alternating passes to 481H/1600 -- distinguishable from one pass (H/4) and two (23H/80).
what_the_unit_laws_found_on_the_way: The three-pass example was written with arithmetic that assumed the honest reporters carry no offset. They do: the model is report = truth + u_r + eps for everybody, and their n_r = 1 shrinks theirs to a fifth. The TEST's arithmetic was corrected to the model rather than the model to the test, and the derivation is written out in the preserved patch. This is also the mechanism behind the five failures, seen small.
